title: Live or Lie: Action-Aware Capsule Multiple Instance Learning for Risk Assessment in Live Streaming Platforms

problem.claim: Risk assessment in live streaming must detect sparse, coordinated malicious behaviors among multiple participants that are concealed within normal activities.

gap.claim: The task is challenging because only room-level labels are available under weak supervision, while timely and accurate detection is needed.

contributions.claim: The work formulates live-streaming-room risk assessment as a Multiple Instance Learning problem, treating each room as a bag and structured user–timeslot capsules as instances.
The instances are user–timeslot capsules representing subsequences of user actions within specific time windows and localized behavioral patterns.

narrative_sequence.summary: Live streaming supports large-scale real-time social interaction.
Sparse coordinated malicious behavior is concealed within normal activity and is difficult to detect promptly and accurately.
The work studies risk assessment in live-streaming rooms under weak supervision with room-level labels.
The task is modeled with Multiple Instance Learning using structured user–timeslot capsules as instances.
The capsules encode time-windowed subsequences of user actions as localized behavioral patterns.

source_observation.claim: Only room-level labels are available while instances are structured user–timeslot capsules.

interpretation.claim: When fine-grained labels are unavailable, a bag-level learning formulation can organize localized behavioral evidence under weak supervision.

application.claim: For other group-level risk or anomaly tasks, represent localized action subsequences as instances and aggregate them under group-level labels.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this approach works beyond live-streaming rooms or under different labeling and behavior distributions.
